question_text:
Some economists point to the Jevons paradox, the phenomenon whereby improved efficiency in using a resource reduces the cost of its use and thereby increases demand, to argue that making household appliances more energy-efficient will not reduce total energy consumption. However, a recent study observed that households that replaced their old appliances with newer, more energy-efficient models did not significantly increase their usage of those appliances. Consequently, improving the energy efficiency of household appliances will lead to a net decrease in total energy consumption.

Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?
